name: Probiotics for body odor

lead: Some people propose probiotics to change body odor through the gut microbiome. A 2020 study explored skin bacteria in the gut microbiome as markers of systemic malodor.
No trials of probiotics for body odor were found in the sources consulted.

paras: The proposed route is the gut microbiome influencing what is excreted through skin. This is not shown by trials in the sources consulted.
Not assessed in the sources consulted.

lead: Probiotics for body odor is the idea that taking probiotic microbes, or altering the gut microbiome, changes how a person smells. Reference sources note that the gut microbiome can affect body odor, citing a 2020 study on cutaneous bacteria in the gut microbiome as biomarkers of systemic malodor.[1]
Grokipedia mentions lactobacilli only as a topical skin treatment that may rebalance skin microbiota, and its citation for that statement appears mismatched, so it is not treated here as evidence.[2]
infobox: Reducing body odor via gut-skin axis

paras: Body odor arises mainly from bacterial activity on sweat gland secretions, with genes, diet and health contributing.[1]
